title: note-template — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one behavioral case for protocol::template::render + protocol::template::supported_tokens — the deterministic note-template variable engine (MYND-188). render(template, ctx) is a PURE FUNCTION: one left-to-right pass over {{token}} placeholders matched case-sensitively against a closed 5-token registry (date, time, title, datetime, weekday). Unknown tokens, format-arg shapes ({{title:foo}}) and stray/unbalanced braces pass through verbatim — that passthrough IS the escape mechanism (there is no dedicated escape syntax). Substituted values are NEVER re-scanned (single pass). The engine reads no clock and no locale: every ctx field arrives pre-formatted from the host, and the engine is byte-transparent including NFD combining sequences (NO unicode normalization). Not an on-disk codec and not cryptographic — it is deterministic cross-client behavior in the password-policy class: every independent client renders the same (template, ctx) to bit-identical output. Two case kinds: 'render' (template + ctx → output bytes) and 'token_registry' (supported_tokens() order/set pin). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/template.rs (main myne repository); contract recorded in decisions.md 2026-06-07 (Note templates).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'note-template/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: render — pin the engine's exact output bytes for one (template, ctx) pair

input_template_utf8_hex.description: The template body as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex, empty allowed). Hex pinning makes the byte sequence the contract, immune to JSON-tooling normalization — load-bearing for the NFD-unicode case.

input_ctx_title_utf8_hex.description: ctx.title as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex, empty allowed — the empty-title case pins that an empty value substitutes as the empty string; the engine has no empty-title policy of its own).

input_ctx_date_utf8_hex.description: ctx.date as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). Host-formatted LOCAL calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD); the engine performs no calendar arithmetic or UTC conversion.

input_ctx_time_utf8_hex.description: ctx.time as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). Host-formatted LOCAL 24-hour time (HH:mm).

input_ctx_datetime_utf8_hex.description: ctx.datetime as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). Host-formatted combined local form.

input_ctx_weekday_utf8_hex.description: ctx.weekday as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). Host-localized day name — the engine carries no locale logic and substitutes the bytes verbatim.

expected_output_utf8_hex.description: The exact UTF-8 bytes render() MUST produce (hex, empty allowed). Bit-identical across implementations — no trailing-whitespace, normalization, or escaping differences tolerated.

informational_template_utf8.description: Human-readable mirror of input_template_utf8_hex. Informational — the runner cross-checks it byte-equal against the hex; the hex is the contract (JSON tooling may silently NFC-normalize this mirror, which a runner cross-check surfaces).

informational_output_utf8.description: Human-readable mirror of expected_output_utf8_hex. Informational — cross-checked against the hex, same caveat as informational_template_utf8.

oneOf.title: token_registry — pin supported_tokens() order and set

expected_tokens.description: The exact return of supported_tokens(), order-sensitive (v1: date, time, title, datetime, weekday — registry order). The SET is load-bearing for render parity (advertised ⇔ substituted, single registry); the ORDER is load-bearing for UI parity (the {{ autocomplete lists tokens in this order).
